performance.cost_breakdown: parts 192.02 USD, filament 24.97 USD (1.00 kg), fasteners ~4.05 USD, wiring 13.70 USD

assumptions: The three modules are the same design at two lengths; the frame is screwed to a flat board (12 mm plywood or MDF, about 450 x 350 mm, not in the parts list).
Lead screws are plain Tr8x8 with brass nuts: cheap and quiet, with some backlash; anti-backlash nuts are a drop-in upgrade.

Clearance is checked with every rod, lead screw, bearing, bushing, coupler and lead nut as its round body with its bore, so each rod through its bushings and each screw through its nut is checked as built; no pair is left out.
Speeds and thrust use the NEMA17's rated torque; at high step rates a stepper's torque falls, so the firmware limits speed to the checked value.
The pen clamp takes pens and markers up to 12 mm; Z lifts the pen between strokes.

notes: Mains side: IEC inlet to the supply's AC terminals with insulated spades, earth wired first, case closed before plugging in. Have it checked if you are not qualified to wire mains.
The ESP32-S3 runs from its USB lead to the PC; its 3V3 feeds the drivers' logic and the home switches. Motor and switch leads run in drag chain or spiral wrap along each module.
